![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14186732/assets/606a6eb139d8e5813f85c608824d8313a97ddaa465b7c05c89173247550a77ee.png)

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$ shown above, determine the measure of $∠C.$
question.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral  must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D & ={360}^{∘} \\ (x+{30}^{∘})+{75}^{∘}+5x+(3x-{15}^{∘}) & ={360}^{∘} \\ 9x+{90}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 9x & ={270}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠C & =5x \\  & =5({30}^{∘}) \\  & ={150}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
